bullets.title: Iran conflict + bond yields dominate: July FOMC now 30% priced for hike
bullets.body: Brent crude surged ~40% in July on Iran/Houthis escalation (Hormuz traffic at 50% of pre-war levels), pushing 2y/10y yields to 18-month highs and 30y near 20-year highs. Markets now price ~30% odds of a 25bp hike at Wednesday's FOMC (up from 12% a week ago), with 39bp of hikes through year-end. 22V and Wolfe both flag the Iran war — not tariffs or macro data — as the dominant market driver; oil near $100 constrains Trump military options while raising ECB/global CB tightening pressure.

bullets.title: Global bond yields hit multi-year highs; 'bond vigilantes' signal regime shift
bullets.body: Bloomberg Global Treasury Index yield rose to 3.68%, highest since the 2008 financial crisis. Bund yields at 3.19% (highest since 2011); long-end US Treasuries at pre-2008 highs. PSC Macro flags fed funds (3.6%) below nominal GDP growth (6.0%) as accommodative, with M2/bank loans accelerating — but bond vigilantes pushing yields higher, and 22V warns the 'higher yields, higher stocks' dynamic could flip.

bullets.title: New Section 301 forced-labor tariffs: minimal inflation impact, ~70bp cumulative PCE
bullets.body: Trump imposed 10-12.5% Section 301 forced-labor tariffs effective July 24, covering 99.4% of US trade. Morgan Stanley and Wolfe both flag minimal incremental inflation risk — MS maintains 70bp cumulative PCE impact forecast (62bp already materialized). Wolfe notes companies didn't cut prices during H1 easing so are unlikely to raise prices now; JPMorgan finds Trump tariff Truth Social posts have lost market impact, with rate vol from such posts ~6x lower post-June 2025 versus April-May 2025.

bullets.title: S&P 500 Q2 earnings: 87% beat rate, +23% y/y EPS growth — but beats not rewarded
bullets.body: Q2 EPS growth running +23% y/y with an 87% beat rate per JPMorgan. Despite strong fundamentals, beats are not being rewarded in stock price — negative FCF and capex anxiety dominate sentiment. Mag-7 fell 4.8% Thursday (largest drop since Liberation Day) with $797B erased from the group on crude spike, credit weakness, and 10y yield pressure.

bullets.title: US PMI data solid; labor market tightens; housing still soft
bullets.body: July S&P Manufacturing PMI edged to 53.8 (expansion), Services PMI jumped +2.4pts with strong new orders. Initial jobless claims printed 187k, lowest since 1969 (down from 209k prior). New home sales rose 1.6% m/m to 628k in June but median prices are down 2.7% y/y and -14% from Oct 2022 peak; housing starts remain rangebound with 9.3 months supply.

bullets.title: Eurozone PMI surges to 5-month high; ECB September hike now near-certain
bullets.body: Eurozone July flash composite PMI rose 1.9pts to 51.9%, but JPMorgan revised 2Q26 GDP up only 0.5pt to 1.0% q/q saar. A second ECB hike in September to 2.5% is now JPM's base case; a third hike is becoming a 'real possibility' if Middle East conflict escalates. Headline CPI expected to accelerate to 3.7% y/y by September; Bund yields at 11-year highs.

bullets.title: Oil volatility: Iran/Houthi risk adds $49/bbl; Brent pulling back below $100
bullets.body: Iran/Houthis geopolitical premium has added an estimated $49/bbl to oil, while demand weakness subtracts ~$10. Brent fell over $4 to ~$96-97/bbl intraday Friday as futures rebounded on oil cooling. Diesel prices are up 10% since July 5, raising input costs across consumer goods. JPMorgan estimates supply disruption could add $7-8/bbl per extra month (Brent to ~$114 on a 3-month disruption scenario).

bullets.title: Hyperscaler capex anxiety: AI bond issuance at $489B YTD; bond repricing threatens equity multiples
bullets.body: Goldman Delta-1 warns reflexivity is the key risk — AI bond repricing is punitive for equity multiples even for hyperscalers with strong balance sheets. AI-related debt issuance reached $489B YTD vs $322B full-year 2025, extending beyond hyperscalers to data centers, semis, and software. Token costs have erased the entire agentic rally and sit at 3.5-month lows alongside hyperscaler index weakness.

bullets.title: MAG-7 earnings next week (MSFT, META, AAPL, AMZN) into FOMC — peak risk event
bullets.body: Next week is peak Q2 season with MSFT, META, AAPL, and AMZN all reporting alongside the July FOMC (Wednesday). Street is on edge about capex guidance — GOOG's -7% drop on capex, META and AMZN face similar anxiety. Any upside capex guidance risks stock declines even with operational beats, per multiple desk commentaries.

bullets.title: AI infrastructure demand remains strong despite near-term AI/momentum factor pressure
bullets.body: 22V notes AI infrastructure beneficiaries are under pressure due to momentum-factor overlap, not fundamental weakness. Hyperscaler capex continues to accelerate; AMD raised its AI accelerator TAM to $1.4T by 2030 (from prior $1T) and DC CPU TAM to $220B. Memory is increasingly the bottleneck for AI builds, with shortage expected to intensify in 2027-2028 and DC memory prices up 25%+ in Q3.

bullets.title: UK services PMI beats sharply at 51.8 vs 49.4 forecast; BoE hawkish tilt expected
bullets.body: UK July services PMI printed 51.8 vs 49.4 forecast, a strong beat. JPMorgan expects BoE to hold at 3.75% next week but tighten the vote split to 6-3 (from 7-2), opening the door for a November hike if wage growth exceeds 3.5%. UK 2Q GDP growth revised up to 1.2% and unemployment down to 4.8%.

bullets.title: El Niño + energy shock could push global food inflation to 6% by early 2027
bullets.body: JPMorgan estimates 81% probability of a super El Niño developing by end-2026, combined with energy shock potentially doubling the historical ~0.7pt food inflation impact to ~1.5pts. Global food inflation is forecast to rise from 2.8% annualized in H1-2026 to 5% in H1-2027, peaking at 6% around April 2027, adding 0.6pt to global headline inflation.

bullets.title: Samsung/SK Hynix to announce 'very large-scale' US chip deals during Korean presidential visit
bullets.body: South Korea's presidential policy chief announced Samsung and SK Hynix will sign major long-term contracts with US technology companies during President Lee Jae-myung's Silicon Valley visit. No specific counterparties disclosed, but the deals are described as 'very large-scale.'

bullets.title: DXY bullish above 100; USD/JPY extending toward 164-165 with no buyer exhaustion
bullets.body: JPMorgan FX technicals flag USD/JPY extending through 163.23 toward a 164.93 measured-move target with no signs of buyer exhaustion and tactical support at 162.50-162.84. DXY maintains bullish outlook above 100 (next resistance 102.72-103.59, longer-term target 105.08). EUR/USD in negative medium-term trend approaching Feb 2025 38.2% retracement at 1.134.

bullets.title: Cargo shipping re-routing via Suez; Red Sea blockade reinforcing oil/supply-chain disruption
bullets.body: Multiple tankers are diverting away from the Red Sea/Bab-el-Mandeb via Suez Canal due to Houthi activity. Houthis announced a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia and claimed attacks on Saudi tankers. SSE SCFI container freight index is down 8% over the past three weeks but remains up 85% YTD.

bullets.title: Semiconductor equipment delivery times doubling; supply chain under pressure
bullets.body: Semiconductor equipment delivery times have reportedly doubled, putting chipmakers under pressure. This constraint is feeding into longer interconnection wait times and advantaging rapid-deployment power providers and Bitcoin-to-datacenter conversion plays for AI campuses.

bullets.title: China launches coordinated AI-chip mobilization via Huawei Ascend; EU adds 14 entities to export list
bullets.body: China is shifting to state-directed AI-chip mobilization led by Huawei Ascend, per Morgan Stanley. Separately, China added 14 European entities to its export control list in retaliation for EU sanctions — escalating tech/trade friction on both sides.

bullets.title: Russell 2000 outperforming S&P by 10.2% YTD; SMID earnings tracking 6% above expectations
bullets.body: Russell 2000 is up 18.5% YTD versus S&P 500 lagging by ~10.2%. Of the 152 Russell 2000 companies that have reported Q2 results (12% of market cap), aggregate earnings are running 6.1% above expectations, suggesting broad earnings health beyond mega-cap.

bullets.title: AI-related debt boom raises hyperscaler ROI questions; token cost deflation a structural threat
bullets.body: Hyperscalers are raising large amounts of debt and equity while trailing returns on both are deteriorating. META's $12B Texas data center financing is clearing at 7%+ yield (40bps tighter than the Louisiana deal). AI token pricing is falling as enterprises choose lower-cost models, threatening the speed of hyperscaler monetization and raising questions about the capital cycle payback.

bullets.title: Section 301 tariffs likely to survive litigation; separate industrial overcapacity probe could add ~150bp to effective rates
bullets.body: Wolfe Research notes courts have historically deferred on Section 301 tariffs, making survival of the new forced-labor duties the base case. A forthcoming separate Section 301 investigation on industrial overcapacity could add ~150bp to global effective tariff rates, though Wolfe still sees minimal aggregate inflationary risk from both combined.
